cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: You Can’t Leave Mid-Prophecy
cards.instruction: Keep someone present until the impossible prediction has been fulfilled, disproved, or responsibly revised.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Keep your coat off. The prophecy says this bell-less tower will ring at noon; I need a witness.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Then sign that before you go. We can officially stop waiting.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My watch is five minutes fast.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then give me four more minutes. I'll fill in our names so only the silence needs witnessing.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 orders coat off, A3 requires signature before leaving, and A5 assigns four more minutes while A prepares the record.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 apparent lateness prompts A3 closure; B4 fast watch means noon is still four minutes away and causes A5 revised wait.

relationship.evidence: B2 gives observation and B4 corrects the reliability of the time, changing the available conclusion.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4 five-minute error exactly rather than adding an unearned obstacle.

specificity.evidence: A1 bell-less tower, noon and witness establish the prediction and task clearly.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 only silence needs witnessing grows from preparing names during the justified extra wait.
